sources.title: Webster, Ogot and Chrétien: The Great Lakes region, 1500 to 1800, UNESCO General History of Africa V
sources.note: Scholarly UNESCO chapter, printed pages 776 to 827, reproduced in this volume segment. Indexed original pages 801 and 827 read; direct fetch failed. Uses broad political development only, not disputed exact reign dates or the older chapter’s unqualified reconstruction of a Chwezi empire.

sources.title: David Schoenbrun, The (in)visible roots of Bunyoro-Kitara and Buganda in the Lakes region: AD 800 to 1300
sources.note: Direct publisher summary read, not the paywalled full chapter. Opening paragraph describes the 1600 to 1800 regional kingdoms, diverse ecological settings and combined technological/agricultural bases.

sources.title: John Sutton, Recovering the African past: looking back from the present, Field Manual for African Archaeology
sources.note: Direct Royal Museum for Central Africa publication by the field archaeologist. Printed page 11, human PDF page 5, figure 2 describes Ntusi around 1000 to 1400 and its refuse mounds. This is earlier regional background, not evidence that the map’s 1783 aggregate existed then.

sources.title: Allen F. Roberts and Marla C. Berns, Striking Iron: The Art of African Blacksmiths (2018)
sources.note: Direct exhibition curators’ article in African Arts 51(1), printed page 79, human PDF page 14. Some Karagwe royal objects traditionally attributed to early nineteenth-century King Ndagara; attribution reported rather than certified individual manufacture.

sources.title: Penn State Palmer Museum: African Brilliance, catalogue 57, milk container
sources.note: Direct university museum entry identifies the object as twentieth-century Baganda and distinguishes Hima parallels and twentieth-century ethnographic documentation. Container care and division of work are documented later examples, not universal eighteenth-century customs.

sources.title: John Hanning Speke, The Discovery of the Source of the Nile (1863), chapter XVI
sources.note: Direct primary travel account, opening of chapter XVI: five-plank vessels, caulking with mbugu cloth, Wanyoro dugouts and trade cargo. Report relates to 1862, after the map window. Speke’s racial theories and disparaging judgments are rejected; specific observations are attributed, not treated as an unfiltered account of all communities.

sources.title: National Library of Uganda / Library of Congress: Biscuit Tin Bible, 1890 to 1896
sources.note: Complete indexed original institutional description read after direct fetch errors. Other Title and Summary attest the Luganda title and English translation; sample is explicitly a catalogue-transcribed title, not independently transcribed interior text. Summary identifies Baganda participation, Duta, portable sections, and 1890 to 1896 production. Metadata contains an erroneous Pilkington birth range, which is not repeated.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Real uncovered HB index ID, 1783 to 1815, alias RI States. Two decoded snapshots share bbox 29.151 to 32.593 E, 4.417 S to 2.286 N, identifying an aggregate in the African Great Lakes rather than all Rift Valley peoples. No new aliases for existing Buganda, Bunyoro, Rwanda or Burundi cards. Earlier Ntusi archaeology and later Karagwe material, 1862 travel, 1890 to 1896 writing and twentieth-century domestic evidence are explicitly dated; none is silently projected onto the short map interval. The bibliography does not identify the exact constituent states intended by the original cartographer; named examples explain regional history rather than asserting precise membership or borders.
